findings.title: Static residual normalization allows strong equations to mask weak equations
findings.details: Previously separate maxima of residual and equation scale mixed strong/weak axes and force/moment units. Existing current patch checks each equation against its own scale. Regression source rejects a tip rotation hidden by a strong axial force.

findings.title: Transient residual aggregation can accept NaN from overflow of finite input states
findings.details: std::max(previous, abs(residual)/scale) preserves previous when overflow produces inf/inf=NaN. Added normalizedResidual rejecting nonfinite residual/scale/ratio for dynamic equilibrium, kinematics and energy. Added synthetic hash-bound two-frame finite-state SDOF energy-overflow regression source.
findings.evidenceBoundary: Actual C++ broker/verifier fixture remains uncompiled/unexecuted. Independent scalar arithmetic and full source-path review establish mechanism and no identified static blocker; they do not prove runtime success.
findings.reachability: Statically reachable through actual ordinary legacy-dynamics broker admission: publishResult -> inspectModel (checkpoint validate/mesh/clock/control, componentwise finite nodal fields) -> readVerifiedModels -> verifier diagnose/field/grid checks -> reference integration -> energyBalance. No NaN is stored; it is generated by quadratic arithmetic after admission. Synthetic checkpoint has finite zero energy ledger and hash-shaped DOF/system identifiers, not a production solver restart certificate.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Rejects nonfinite derived residuals instead of treating them as passing; ordinary finite positive control and existing transient cases must remain passing at unchanged thresholds.

findings.title: Initial-condition reconciliation ignores enabled state and component metadata
findings.conditions: Leave initial values unchanged but disable a nonzero component, change units/key units, or add samples to non-first components. Old signature used values and only first-component table length; solver skips disabled components.
findings.impact: diagnose could report matching ProblemSpec for different effective initial state. Verifier modelSupport could therefore accept metadata inconsistent with its independent initial reference; other response checks may still reject real mismatched solves.
findings.certainty: Concrete omitted-field comparison and producer skip-disabled behavior inspected. No claim that every mutated production solve would pass all verifier metrics.
findings.fix: Bind component count, variable, enabled, SI unit, keyType, keyUnits and complete per-component time keys in expected and actual IC signatures.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Previously admitted malformed/non-SI/disabled/time-table IC metadata now fails; intended candidate-generated SI single-time initial states remain unchanged.
findings.regression: Four IC families each have an unchanged positive and disabled/value-unit/key-unit/shifted-key/extra-sample negatives. Source only.
findings.platformValidation: Linux and Windows Qt6: compile/run focused mechanics test and existing verifier transient RAM/RBM cases; expected metadata issue and status error on every negative, positives unchanged.

findings.title: Mesh-refinement proposal narrows an unbounded finite authorized maximum before clamping
findings.conditions: A non-study authorization admits an integer-valued finite double maximum greater than INT_MAX (including DBL_MAX), while current mesh is valid. A measured precision failure requests authorized mesh refinement.
findings.impact: int(maximum) is outside representable range before qMin, causing undefined C++ conversion rather than the intended bounded doubling; direct helper also doubled current in signed int.
findings.certainty: Authorization accepts this range and helper cast is unguarded in old source. Platform-specific undefined result was not executed or asserted.
findings.fix: Compute minimum/next doubled proposal in double, reject an unrepresentable resulting candidate, then narrow.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Representable ranges and fixed physics/tolerance unchanged; removes undefined behavior for large upper bounds.
findings.regression: Real authorization accepts caps 6, 8, DBL_MAX and proposal returns 6, 8, 8 from baseline4; exhausted cap fails without output mutation.
findings.platformValidation: Run focused and full experiment target on GCC/Clang/MSVC; optional float-cast-overflow sanitizer only when builds are authorized.

findings.impact: Positive declaration fixture fails path preflight before reaching its intended schema checks. This is test portability, not a demonstrated product defect.
findings.fix: Use a QTemporaryDir-derived absolute sourcePath; no source script is created or executed.
findings.compatibilityRisk: None intended: keeps Windows absolute path validity and makes Linux fixture absolute; fake source/dependency/environment identities remain declaration-only.
findings.platformValidation: Run externalDeclarationShape on Linux and Windows with redirected TMP paths; positive roundtrip passes and existing four malformed declarations fail.

findings.title: Modal residual aggregation accepts overflowed finite mode vectors as zero residual
findings.conditions: Four-element fixed/free axial rod, consistent-mass first discrete eigenpair. Scale finite sin(j*pi/8) mode by1e308: Kphi and omega^2 Mphi overflow in each free row, residual becomes NaN, std::max preserves0, maximumScale becomes inf, old eigenError=0/inf=0.
findings.impact: Hash-valid finite modal fields and plausible frequency can pass modalResidual even though no finite residual certificate exists. Modal branch has no energy gate to block this case.
findings.certainty: Full ordinary modal broker->verification path read. Independent stdlib matrix arithmetic reproduces normal residual2.400134025523869e-17 and overflow old-pass/new-fail. C++ fixture unexecuted.
findings.fix: Require each accumulated modal row residual/scale to be finite, then use existing finite-safe normalizer. Original normwise normalization, 1e-6 limit and physical operators retained.
findings.regression: Independent exact discrete eigenpair positive and scaled finite overflow negative published/read through actual broker. No production solve needed by this test.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Only nonfinite derived certificates change from pass to fail; valid normal-scale eigenpairs retain prior threshold. Huge arbitrary amplitudes must be represented at a finite arithmetic scale before acceptance.
findings.platformValidation: Compile/run focused modal regression and existing rod/beam modal suite under IEEE finite semantics on Linux/Windows; negative identity/model/fields/support/frequency/modeShape pass, modalResidual fail.

findings.title: Periodic v1 checkpoint recovery incorrectly requires adjacent accepted sequences
findings.conditions: Ordinary v1 writer publishes full MODEL periodically (up to10 accepted steps/1s). Interrupted publication from oldLatest10 to candidate20 leaves a valid PENDING rollback; old unconditional oldLatest+1==candidate rejected it.
findings.impact: Legitimate periodic checkpoint rollback/recovery fails, even with valid context and transaction hashes. v2 trace still commits every accepted record and requires adjacency.
findings.certainty: Coordinator native-cli finding independently checked against publisher due predicate and application validatePointer/inspect logic. No C++ recovery executed.
findings.fix: Restrict adjacency guard to traceMode; retain existing strict-old-before-candidate, old-lastvalid order, context/schema/hash/transaction basename and writer lease checks.
findings.regression: Existing tst_piezo_accepted_trace target gains7 Provider-free storage cases: v1 gap/adjacent positives, equal/backwards/cross-context negatives, v2 adjacent positive/gap negative; restores and repeated restore then finish are asserted.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Restores intended periodic v1 behavior, no schema/physical/identity changes; storage fixture opaque MODEL bytes are not a native physics certificate.
findings.platformValidation: Run checkpointRecoverySequencePolicy and native-cli periodic publication regression after authorization on Linux/Windows; failures must preserve marker and both pointers byte-for-byte.

findings.title: Axial bridge test comparison silently accepts nonfinite expected operands
findings.conditions: close(finite,NaN) sees abs(NaN)>scale as false; close(finite,infinity) compares infinity>infinity as false. Old helper checks only actual a finite.
findings.impact: A nonfinite expected oracle or operator value can make a scalar/vector test comparison pass. This is a test assertion defect, not evidence that the production source emits those values.
findings.fix: Require both operands finite, retain existing finite-value tolerance; new numericComparisonRejectsNonfiniteOperands covers equal/near positives, finite mismatch and NaN/+inf/-inf on each side.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Only invalid nonfinite comparisons change; production code/operators/thresholds untouched.

findings.title: Holdout canonical JSON negatives have alternative rejection paths
findings.conditions: Escaped-public fixture changes file bytes without signing their digest, so removing canonical guard would still fail public_cases_digest_mismatch. Following newline-key negative leaves invalid public cases in place, so another rejection can mask a missing key canonical guard.
findings.impact: Regression could stay green after loss of the precise canonical-byte protection it intends to test. Production guard order207-271 inspected only as fixture context; no product vulnerability claimed.
findings.fix: Optional exact-public-bytes resign helper signs matching digest and persists those exact bytes; assert invalid_canonical_json. Restore canonical public cases plus a passing control before newline-key case, repin exact newline bytes, assert same canonical error, then restore passing canonical key.
findings.compatibilityRisk: Existing fixture resign() defaults remain canonical and unchanged; no production crypto/canonicalization/trust rules changed.
